correctness.rationale: For nonzero x, Mx^[2] is uniform on nonzero vectors, giving mean one. Distinct collinear x,y cannot both be fixed. Independent source/target vector pairs have joint probability 1/((q^n-1)(q^n-q)). For odd q, support-r x contribute (q-1)(2^r-2)/2 square-dependent independent y; summing gives exactly (q-1)((2q-1)^n-2q^n+1)/2. In even characteristic Frobenius squaring preserves linear dependence, giving zero deficit. Ten independently enumerated small profiles, including GF(4), agree with exact mean/variance. Dimension one treated separately. Finite tests do not replace the general proof.

value.rationale: The exact finite-field variance is the first nontrivial fluctuation beyond the established mean-one statement for random perfect evolution structures. It distinguishes odd and even characteristic, quantifies a positive finite-field departure from the symmetric-group fixed-point second moment, and has a natural large-field limit compatible with the conjectured generic-Galois behavior. The odd-characteristic formula holds in every dimension >=2 and every odd prime power, not an arbitrary finite slice.
